meta.title: Hosea the Prophet: God's Love is Timeless
meta.verseText: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart.
meta.theme: No matter the time or place, God's love never stops. Like a caring parent, God loved His people in the past, loves us today, and will love us forever.

questions.text: Who was Hosea?
questions.hint: It means someone who listened to God and shared His message.
questions.explanation: Hosea was a prophet, which means he listened to God and shared God's message with the people.

questions.text: What was a prophet's job?
options: To listen to God and share His message
questions.hint: It has to do with God's words.
questions.explanation: A prophet listened to God and shared God's message with the people, just like Hosea did.

questions.text: What is the Big Idea we learned this week?
questions.hint: It has to do with time and love.
questions.explanation: The Big Idea is that God's love is timeless. Every hour, every day, God's love for us ticks on!

questions.text: What message did God give Hosea to tell the people?
questions.hint: It is a message about God's love.
questions.explanation: God gave Hosea this message: 'Tell My people I still love them.' God never stopped loving them.

questions.text: In Hosea 11:1-4, God's love was compared to a loving _____ who cares for a child.
questions.hint: Think of a mom or dad who lifts a little child to their cheek.
questions.explanation: God said He loved His people like a caring parent who teaches a child to walk and lifts them to their cheek.

questions.text: According to Hosea 11, God taught His people to _____.
questions.hint: It's something little children learn to do with their legs.
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:3 says it was God who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by the arms, like a loving parent.

questions.text: True or False: God stopped loving His people when they walked away from Him.
questions.hint: Remember, God's love is timeless.
questions.explanation: False! Even when His people walked away, God did not stop loving them. God said, 'I will not stop loving them.'

questions.text: What did God's people keep forgetting to do?
questions.hint: It's about paying attention to God.
questions.explanation: God's people kept forgetting to listen to Him and made wrong choices that walked them away from God.

questions.text: Our memory verse says God has made everything beautiful in its _____.
questions.hint: It's what clocks measure.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 3:11 says, 'He has made everything beautiful in its time.'

questions.text: The memory verse says God has set _____ in the human heart.
questions.hint: It means forever and ever, with no end.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 3:11 says, 'He has also set eternity in the human heart.' Eternity means forever.

questions.text: Which book of the Bible is our memory verse from?
questions.hint: It starts with the letter E.
questions.explanation: Our memory verse is from Ecclesiastes 3:11.

questions.text: Where in the Bible do we find the story of Hosea's message about God's love?
questions.hint: The book is named after the prophet himself.
questions.explanation: Our Bible story comes from Hosea 11:1-11, in the book named after the prophet Hosea.

questions.text: True or False: When we make wrong choices, things can become hard.
questions.hint: God's people had hard days when they walked away.
questions.explanation: True. God's people made choices that hurt them and had hard days, but God still loved them.

questions.text: Did God give up on His people?
options: No, He wanted them to come back
questions.hint: God's love is timeless.
questions.explanation: No! God did not give up. He said, 'I will not stop loving them,' and He wanted His people to come back to Him.

questions.text: In the lesson, we pretended the room was a _____ to travel to Hosea's time.
questions.hint: We counted down 3, 2, 1 and blasted to the past!
questions.explanation: We pretended the room was a time machine and traveled back to the time of Hosea.

questions.text: What craft did the kids make to remember God's love is timeless?
questions.hint: It tells time and ticks on and on.
questions.explanation: The kids made a clock out of paper plates, pipe cleaners, and heart stickers to remember God's love ticks on every hour and every day.

questions.text: Hebrews 10:23 tells us we can hold onto God's promise because God is _____.
questions.hint: It means God always keeps His promises.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:23 shows us God is faithful and keeps His promises, so we can trust that His love is timeless.

questions.text: What does it mean that God's love is 'timeless'?
options: It never ends, no matter the time
questions.hint: Think past, present, and future.
questions.explanation: Timeless means God's love never ends. God loved His people in the past, loves us today, and will love us forever.

questions.text: True or False: God only loves us when we make good choices.
questions.hint: God loved His people even when they walked away.
questions.explanation: False. God loves us no matter what, even when we mess up. His love does not depend on us being perfect.

questions.text: In Hosea 11:1, God said, 'Out of Egypt I called my _____.'
questions.hint: God spoke about His people like His own child.
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:1 says, 'When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.'

questions.text: The lesson says God loved His people like one who lifts a little child to the _____.
questions.hint: It's a soft part of your face.
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:4 describes God as one who lifts a little child to the cheek, showing His tender, loving care.

questions.text: How can you show God that you love Him?
options: Pray, listen to the Bible, sing and dance
questions.hint: The lesson gave three ways during worship.
questions.explanation: We can say 'I love you' to God by praying, listening to the Bible story, and singing and dancing to worship Him.

questions.text: What is one way you can share God's love with someone this week?
options: Show kindness and tell them God loves them
questions.hint: Think about being kind, just like God is kind to us.
questions.explanation: We can share God's timeless love by being kind, helping others, and telling them how much God loves them.

questions.text: If a friend makes a wrong choice, what does Hosea's story teach us to do?
options: Keep loving them, like God does
questions.hint: Remember how God treated His people when they walked away.
questions.explanation: Just as God kept loving His people even when they walked away, we can keep loving others even when they make mistakes.

questions.text: True or False: When we mess up, we can ask God to forgive us.
questions.hint: Think about the prayer at the end of the lesson.
questions.explanation: True! In the closing prayer we said sorry and asked God to forgive us. God loves us and forgives us when we ask.

questions.text: How might God speak to us today?
options: Through the Bible, prayer, and people who love Him
questions.hint: Think about God's time-travel guide and talking to Him.
questions.explanation: God can speak to us today through the Bible, through prayer, and through people who share His message, just like He spoke through prophets.

questions.text: What did the heart stickers on the clock craft remind the kids of?
options: God's love ticking on every hour
questions.hint: Hearts stand for love, and clocks tell time.
questions.explanation: The heart stickers on the clock reminded kids that God's love ticks on every hour and every day.

questions.text: The people worshiped false gods called the _____ instead of the one true God.
questions.hint: The name starts with B and appears in Hosea 11:2.
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:2 says they sacrificed to the Baals, which were false gods, instead of worshiping the one true God.

questions.text: True or False: Hosea's story shows God loves His people in the past, today, and forever.
questions.hint: That's what timeless means!
questions.explanation: True! Hosea's story reminds us God loved His people in the past, loves us today, and will love us forever.

questions.text: Why do you think God spoke through prophets like Hosea?
options: To share His love and messages with the people
questions.hint: A prophet's job was to share God's message.
questions.explanation: God spoke through prophets so His people could hear His messages, especially the message that He still loved them.

questions.text: Where did God call His son out of, according to Hosea 11:1?
questions.hint: It's the land where God's people had once been slaves.
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:1 says, 'Out of Egypt I called my son,' remembering how God rescued His people from Egypt.

questions.text: What can you do this week to remember that God's love never stops?
options: Look at a clock and thank God for His timeless love
Only think about it on Sunday
questions.hint: Think about the clock craft you made.
questions.explanation: Every time you see a clock ticking, you can remember and thank God that His love ticks on every hour and every day.

story.summary: Long ago, God chose a man named Hosea to be a prophet. A prophet listens to God and shares God's message with the people. God loved His people, Israel, very much, but they kept forgetting to listen to Him. They made wrong choices and walked away from God, even worshiping false gods. God could have stopped loving them, but He did not. Instead, God gave Hosea a message: 'Tell My people I still love them.' In Hosea 11, God said He loved His people like a caring parent who teaches a child to walk and lifts them gently to their cheek. Even when the people walked away and had hard days, God did not give up on them. He said, 'I will not stop loving them,' and He wanted them to come back to Him. Hosea's story reminds us that God's love is timeless — He loved His people in the past, loves us today, and will love us forever. Just like a clock that keeps ticking, God's love ticks on every hour and every day.

scenes.title: Meet Hosea the Prophet
scenes.description: Long ago, God chose Hosea to be a prophet. A prophet listens to God and shares His message with the people. We climbed into our pretend time machine and counted down 3, 2, 1 to blast to the past and meet Hosea!

scenes.title: The People Walk Away
scenes.description: God loved His people, Israel, very much, but they kept forgetting to listen to Him. They made wrong choices, worshiped the false gods called Baals, and walked away from God. When we make wrong choices, things can become hard.

scenes.title: God's Loving Message
scenes.description: God gave Hosea a message: 'Tell My people I still love them.' In Hosea 11, God said He loved His people like a caring parent who taught them to walk and lifted them gently to the cheek. He even reminded them He called His son out of Egypt.

scenes.title: God Never Gives Up
scenes.description: Even when His people walked away, God did not give up on them. He said, 'I will not stop loving them,' and wanted them to come back. God's love is timeless!

scenes.title: Living Out God's Timeless Love
scenes.description: Back in today's time, we learned that God's love never stops for us either. We can love God back by praying, listening to the Bible, and singing. And we can share His timeless love with others all week long — just like the clock we made keeps ticking!
